style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: Arjuna admits he does not know if fighting is better
candidates.evidence: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः

candidates.angle: He does not know who will win the war
candidates.evidence: यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः

candidates.angle: He does not wish to live after killing his kin
candidates.evidence: यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः

en.intro: Arjuna stands between two armies with his bow lowered. He admits he cannot tell which is better, or who will win.
en.notice: Arjuna admits he cannot tell whether fighting or not fighting is better, or which side would win.
en.next: He now asks Krishna to tell him with certainty what is best, because he is confused about his duty.
en.meaning: We do not know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight. We do not even know whether we will conquer them or they us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we do not wish to live after killing them.

hi.intro: अर्जुन दो सेनाओं के बीच अपना धनुष नीचे किए खड़े हैं। वे मान लेते हैं कि वे नहीं जानते कि लड़ना बेहतर है या न लड़ना, और जीत किसकी होगी।
hi.meaning: हम यह भी नहीं जानते कि हमलोगोंके लिये युद्ध करना और न करना इन दोनोंमेंसे कौनसा अत्यन्त श्रेष्ठ है और हमें इसका भी पता नहीं है कि हम उन्हें जीतेंगे अथवा वे हमें जीतेंगे । जिनको मारकर हम जीना भी नहीं चाहते, वे ही धृतराष्ट्र के सम्बन्धी हमारे सामने खड़े हैं ॥
hi.notice: सुनिए कतरत् शब्द, जो दोनों में से। अर्जुन सही और गलत में से नहीं चुन रहे, वे लड़ना और न लड़ना में से चुन रहे हैं, और उन्हें नहीं पता कि दोनों में से कौन सा बेहतर है।
hi.next: वे अब श्रीकृष्ण से निश्चित रूप से पूछते हैं कि उनके लिए क्या सबसे अच्छा है, क्योंकि उनका मन धर्म के बारे में उलझ गया है।

en.intro: Arjuna stands between two armies with his bow lowered. He admits he cannot tell which is better, or who will win.
en.body: We do not know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight. We do not even know whether we will conquer them or they us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we do not wish to live after killing them. Arjuna admits he cannot tell whether fighting or not fighting is better, or which side would win. He now asks Krishna to tell him with certainty what is best, because he is confused about his duty.
